entry.pattern: coordination[XP₁ ... gap + Coordinator + XP₂ ...] + shared right-edge constituent

1.definition: Expresses shared right-edge material once while contrasting what precedes it.
1.details: In She knew of but never mentioned the proposal, the proposal completes both knew of and mentioned. Its functions differ across the two coordinates. Delay can foreground the contrast between the predicates.

examples.note: Constructed after the CGEL model with a PP complement in one coordinate and a direct object in the other.

examples.form: I am [interested in but worried about the new plan].
examples.note: Constructed example where different prepositions precede the delayed NP.

relatedConstructions.notes: The first parts occur in a coordinate structure.

grounds.note: Lists Shared_completion, also known as right-node raising.
Shows different syntactic functions for the delayed element.

projection.target: The single pronounced NP can satisfy two distinct local frames. The preposition inside the first coordinate can select that NP even though the second frame takes a direct object.
projection.evidence: The CGEL examples control which constituent is delayed and show different complement selections. FrameNet names the Shared_completion construction.

curious.title: One ending shared by two halves
curious.summary: In a linked pair of phrases, the shared last part can be said once, at the very end.
curious.body:
In She knew of but never mentioned the proposal, the phrase the proposal finishes both parts of the sentence. She knew of the proposal, and she never mentioned the proposal. Saying it only once, at the end, lets the speaker set the two verbs against each other.

The shared ending does a different job in each half. After knew of it is the object of a preposition, and after mentioned it is a direct object. This dictionary treats the analysis as provisional.

examples.text: She [knew of but never mentioned the proposal].
I am [interested in but worried about the new plan].

curious.try: Combine two short sentences about the same thing, such as I like it and I fear it, into one with a single it at the end. Which parts come before it?

teacher.summary: Helps explain right-edge sharing, where a final phrase completes two coordinated parts, as in knew of but never mentioned the proposal.
teacher.explain: In this construction, the first parts occur in a coordinate structure and a single constituent at the right edge is expressed once. In She knew of but never mentioned the proposal, the proposal completes both knew of and mentioned, though its functions differ across the two coordinates: it is the complement of a preposition in one and a direct object in the other. In I am interested in but worried about the new plan, different prepositions precede the delayed NP. Delay can foreground the contrast between the predicates. The pronounced NP satisfies two distinct local frames. The analysis is provisional.
teacher.terms: Right-edge sharing is sometimes called right-node raising.

examples.text: She [knew of but never mentioned the proposal].
I am [interested in but worried about the new plan].

contrasts.text: She knew of but never mentioned the proposal.
contrasts.note: The shared NP is a prepositional complement in one coordinate and a direct object in the other.

contrasts.text: I am [interested in but worried about the new plan].
contrasts.note: Different prepositions precede the delayed noun phrase.

watch_for: A learner might think the proposal is the direct object of both verbs, when it follows the preposition of in the first part.
A learner might expect each half to have its own ending, when the shared ending is said once.
teacher.activity: Give students pairs of sentences about one object (I like it. I fear it.) and prepositional pairs (interested in, worried about). They combine each pair into one sentence with one shared ending and mark what comes before it in each part.
